newsitem.title: USA: Perot to sue over exclusion from election debates.
newsitem.headline: Perot to sue over exclusion from election debates.

text.p: Reform party presidential candidate Ross Perot will file a federal lawsuit later this week challenging the Commission on Presidential Debates' decision to exclude him from campaign debates, the Perot campaign announced on Tuesday.

"We will file suit in federal court this week," Perot campaign National Coordinator Russell Verney told a press conference after the bipartisan panel recommended that only President Bill Clinton and Republican challenger Bob Dole participate in the nationally televised debates.

"We will seek a temporary restraining order against the debates occurring until we can get a full and fair hearing," Verney said of the Perot campaign suit, which he said should be ready to be filed on Thursday or Friday.

The suit will be filed in U.S. District Court in Washington, he said, and will seek to get the Federal Election Commission -- a government agency -- to enforce its rules that sponsors of debates use objective criteria to decide if candidates qualify to participate.

The Perot campaign said it met all of the bipartisan commission's objective rules for participation but that the commission decided to exclude Perot using a subjective test based on polls and discussions with journalists and political consultants.

The commission said it recommended against Perot participating because only Clinton and Dole "have a realistic chance as set forth in our criteria to be elected the next president of the United States."
